title: Symmetric monoidal transport to a prescribed tensor bifunctor
statement: For a symmetric monoidal category A, a bifunctor T:A×A→A and a natural isomorphism from the original tensor bifunctor to T, there is a symmetric monoidal structure on the same category whose uncurried tensor is literally T. The identity equivalence in either direction is strong braided monoidal. Its tensor constraints are the given comparison and its inverse.

source.place: Monoidal.induced, fromInducedMonoidal, SymmetricCategory.ofFullyFaithful; explicit conjugation of constraints

proof.text: Define tensor objects and tensor maps using T; conjugate associators and unitors by the given isomorphism. Naturality of the isomorphism gives the three map compatibility equations.

source.place: Monoidal.induced, fromInducedMonoidal, SymmetricCategory.ofFullyFaithful; explicit conjugation of constraints

proof.text: Apply Mathlib Monoidal.induced to the identity functor with these explicit data. Functor extensionality and functoriality of T prove equality of bifunctors, including maps.

source.place: Monoidal.induced, fromInducedMonoidal, SymmetricCategory.ofFullyFaithful; explicit conjugation of constraints

proof.text: Pull back symmetry along the fully faithful strong identity functor. Check its braiding by applying the functor and cancelling the inverse tensorator. The monoidal inverse is braided by the counit square and faithfulness.
